candidates.teachingObjective: After losing the ball while still standing as second pivot on the left six, first recover out to the left wing lane to deny the same-side outlet — do not stay wrestling on six or chase the middle ball.
candidates.startingGeometry: LW already deep as second pivot on left half of six; first pivot still left; LB high after failed drive; ball just lost near left 9m; opposing right wing already sprinting into the empty left wing lane.
candidates.whyBecauseLW: This defensive problem only exists because the LW entered as second pivot in the preceding attack (pilot continuity with 945). Normal wing defence never starts from that body position.
candidates.primaryCue: Possession lost + opp right wing sprinting into the empty left wing lane while you are still on the six.
candidates.decisionFork: Sprint out to cut the same-side wing outlet vs chase central ball vs stay wrestling on six vs wait.
candidates.optimal: Sprint out to the left wing lane and close the first outlet path to their right wing.
candidates.goodConditional: Stay one beat inside only if a teammate already owns the wing lane by body and call.
candidates.risky: Chase the central ball carrier because the steal looks more urgent.
candidates.poor: Keep wrestling on the six as if the attack is still alive.
candidates.closestRwGold: scn_bank_930 (return through correct lane after missed shot — normal recovery start, not second-pivot start)
candidates.closestOtherGold: scn_bank_927 (deny fast restart from sideline nearest position)
candidates.duplicateAssessment: Not duplicate. Same broad transition theme as 930/927, but cue/decision/start geometry differ: offensive second-pivot start → reopen defensive wing lane.
candidates.mirrorTest: PASS under sequence clause: abstract wing-recovery principle can flip, but the reason the decision occurs is LW second-pivot preceding position. Fails only if judged as pure side-label wing defence; it is not — start is inside after LW entry.

candidates.teachingObjective: After a second-pivot entry with own goalkeeper out, a turnover makes empty-own-goal cover the first job when you are already the nearest body on the six — do not automatic-sprint to the wing.
candidates.startingGeometry: Own GK out (empty own). LW already second pivot on left half of six from the 7v6 entry. Turnover. Opp centre has the ball ~12–14m looking at the empty goal. Opp right wing is also wide, but a teammate is closer to that wing than you are to empty-goal cover if you leave.
candidates.whyBecauseLW: Only the LW who entered as second pivot is already inside near the empty-goal lane. A wing who stayed wide faces the opposite recovery geometry. This is the defensive consequence of the LW offensive empty-own/second-pivot action.
candidates.primaryCue: Empty own goal live + ball carrier looking at goal + you are nearest body from second-pivot spot; wing is secondary because a teammate is nearer that lane.
candidates.decisionFork: Fill empty-goal lane now vs sprint to wing vs chase ball carrier from behind vs freeze.
candidates.optimal: Sprint between ball and empty goal immediately and force a later decision.
candidates.goodConditional: Sprint to the wing only if a teammate already fills the empty-goal lane and calls that cover.
candidates.risky: Sprint to the wing because ‘that is my job’ while the empty goal is still open.
candidates.poor: Stand near the six and protest the turnover.
candidates.closestRwGold: None for empty-own defence. Nearest attack empty-own: scn_bank_879 / 912. Transition defence nearest: scn_bank_931 (stop first wave between ball and goal — not empty-own, not second-pivot start).
candidates.closestOtherGold: Architecture family lw_def_empty_own_after_turnover (missing in RW Gold defence).
candidates.duplicateAssessment: Not duplicate of RW Gold. 931 shares ‘body between ball and goal’ language but lacks empty-own game state and second-pivot preceding position.
candidates.mirrorTest: PASS under sequence clause: empty-goal fill can flip for RW, but occurrence and body-priority invert because LW entered as second pivot with GK out. Not a normal wing-lane set-defence mirror.
